subject: Performance SLO & Private VPC network qualification — Acme Retail
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLO & Private VPC network qualification

Thanks again for the call earlier, Alex — great to meet you and the Acme team. Quick recap + next steps so we can move toward a short validation window.

Key goals we captured on the call:
- Latency: p95 < 150ms for streaming responses (typical message size ~1–2KB).
- Throughput: sustained 200 requests/sec for inference fan-out, spike to 400rps for short bursts.
- Concurrency: expected 40–60 concurrent connections during peak.
- Streaming: client uses SSE/websocket-style streaming; we need stable 100ms chunk latencies.

Environment notes you shared:
- Production will run in Acme private VPC (AWS) behind Transit Gateway; traffic will egress through NATs and an approved set of IPs.
- You have a standard perimeter VPN and also an option to create VPC peering if required.

Action items (proposed):
1) Acme: share network topology (diagram) and the list of egress NAT IPs + any firewall rules that would need to be opened to Redwood test-pods.
2) Acme: confirm whether VPC peering is an option for the test window or if we need to go through VPN/Transit Gateway.
3) Redwood: we will propose a short test plan (smoke + load) and a canary SLO for the first run; we will need a 2–3 hour test window for the load run.
4) Technical: Jordan will follow up with specific traceroute/connection checks and preferred ports/ip ranges.

If you can share the network diagram and egress IPs (or a point of contact for networking) this week we can draft the test plan and proposed times.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0124

Attachments: none in this message

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Network Ops <netops@acme-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLO & Private VPC network qualification

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming details from our side:

- Latency target: we want p95 <= 150ms for streaming segments, p99 not to exceed 350ms in normal conditions.
- Expected load: baseline 200rps, can spike to ~400rps for short campaigns.
- Concurrency: design target 50 active concurrent connections; some internal services burst higher but we expect the RL path to be in that window.
- Streaming: we use a websocket-based client that streams 100–300 byte chunks; ordering is important.

Notes on network:
- Production traffic will traverse Transit Gateway. We currently do not have a dedicated VPC peering established with vendors by default; we can stand up peering for partners on a case-by-case basis if needed.
- We will provide an egress IP list for NAT (attached), and our network team can provide a diagram (we'll upload to the Drive link).
- For the test window, we can either open firewall rules for Redwood test IPs (preferred) or do a temporary VPN connection.

I'll loop in our netops alias (netops@acme-retail.com) who will share the diagram and egress IPs. Expect those docs by EOD tomorrow.

Alex Chen
Senior Infrastructure PM | Acme Retail
alex.chen@acme-retail.com | +1 (212) 555-0189

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLO & Private VPC network qualification

Alex — thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround. A few technical clarifications from our side before we plan a test window:

1) Can you confirm expected internal latency budgets from your edge to the target subnets (one-way ms)? Even rough numbers help (e.g., 5–20ms).
2) MTU and any jumbo frame settings on the path (we've seen fragmentation impact stream chunking).
3) Will your Transit Gateway preserve source IPs (so we can do client IP allowlisting) or will traffic NAT inside your cloud? If NAT occurs, please provide the egress IP list for allowlisting.
4) For the initial validation, would Acme allow a temporary VPC peering to our test VPC? If not, VPN is fine but peering reduces variability.
5) Preferred ports: 443 for TLS; do you need us to use a different port or client cert?
6) Maintenance windows / <48h planned changes in next two weeks?

We also request a network contact (name + best contact) to coordinate traceroutes and a small-scale test pod that will run a handful of concurrent connections for 30–60 minutes. If you can provide the network-diagram.png and the egress-ips.csv that Alex mentioned that would be perfect.

If you prefer, we can do a quick 30-min network handoff call with your netops to review the diagram and the proposed test inbound rules.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0171

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme-retail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Network Ops <netops@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLO & Private VPC network qualification

Jordan / Marissa — sending the items we discussed. See attachments: network-diagram.png, egress-ips.csv, vpn-config-template.txt. A few notes inline:

- Internal latency: edge -> target subnets typically 6–12ms one-way in us-east-1; cross-az variance up to ~4ms.
- MTU: standard 1500 across the path; no jumbo frames.
- Transit Gateway behavior: we do source NAT for traffic traversing TGW to third-party vendors. The egress-ips.csv contains the NAT IPs you can allowlist.
- Peering: we can set up a temporary VPC peering for the validation window — requires a ticket to netops but usually 48–72h lead time.
- Ports: TLS on 443 is fine; we do not require mutual TLS for initial tests.
- Maintenance: nothing planned in the next 2 weeks.

Network contact: Priya Natarajan (priya.natarajan@acme-retail.com), Netops Lead — she'll coordinate the peering ticket or temporary firewall rules.

Proposed next steps:
1) You (Redwood) propose a 2–3 hour test window next week; we can reserve a dedicated time and create a ticket for peering if you want that route.
2) If peering is requested, we'll start the ticket now; if not, we will provide firewall openings for Redwood test IPs (see egress file).

Let me know which path you prefer and we'll book a time.

Thanks,
Alex

Attachments: network-diagram.png (image), egress-ips.csv (csv), vpn-config-template.txt (text)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Private VPC network qualification — next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks for the artifacts and the quick answers. Proposed plan from Redwood:

1) Test plan (summary):
   - Smoke (10 min): basic TLS handshake + single-stream correctness.
   - Functional streaming validation (20 min): 10 concurrent streams, verify chunk ordering and latency distribution.
   - Load run (90 min): ramp to 200rps sustained, 5-minute spike to 400rps; collect p50/p95/p99 for per-chunk latency and end-to-end response times.
   - Canary SLOs: p95 per-chunk < 150ms; p99 end-to-end < 350ms; error rate < 0.5%.

2) Network approach: we prefer temporary VPC peering to reduce NAT variability. If Acme can open a peering ticket (48–72h lead) we'll go that route; otherwise we'll use your egress IPs and you can open firewall rules for Redwood test IPs.

3) Test data and access: Jordan/Ethan will need a test subnet and an allowlist for our pod IPs or the peering details (route table entries). We'll also provide a small test harness and a short doc with traceroute/troubleshooting commands to run if we see unexpected latency.

4) Proposed windows: Wed 2027-08-18 10:00–13:00 PDT (peering path preferred) OR Thu 2027-08-19 09:00–12:00 PDT (VPN/NAT path). Please confirm which window works and whether Priya can open the peering ticket if we go that route.

If that works, Jordan will coordinate the pre-check traceroutes the day before and share the test harness.

Thanks — looking forward to validating the SLOs.

Best,
--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0124
